production.note: US model years. First: Hyundai's media alert is headed '2022 Elantra N Makes North American Debut'; its Spanish-language launch release refers to the 'ELANTRA N 2022' (hyundai-us-2022-elantra-n-release-es). Still on sale: Hyundai Motor America's consumer site showed the '2026 ELANTRA N' specifications on 2026-10-01 (hyundai-us-2026-elantra-n-specs).

transmission.note: '6-speed manual transmission' (standard) and 'N 8-speed Wet Dual Clutch Transmission (DCT) with paddle shifters' (optional). The 2022 launch release names the same pair (hyundai-us-2022-elantra-n-release-es).

powerHp.note: Quote: "Horsepower (HP): 276 @ 5500 ~ 6000". 2022 media alert (hyundai-us-2022-elantra-n-nyias): "2.0-liter Turbocharged, "Flat Power" Tuned Engine Delivers 276 HP/289 lb.-ft. Torque". The 2026 consumer page gives 'Horsepower @ RPM (ULEV/PZEV) 276 @ 5500 ~ 6000'. N Grin Shift gives a temporary 286 hp (the Spanish-language release: '...incrementando la potencia del motor hasta 286 caballos de fuerza', hyundai-us-2022-elantra-n-release-es); the record uses the continuous rating.

weightLb.note: 6-speed manual, 2023 model. Quote (Hyundai's 2023 Elantra line sheet, raw text): "Curb (lbs.) IVT MT DCT ... - 3,186 3,296", the final column (Elantra N: no IVT, manual, DCT). Hyundai's 2026 consumer page labels the same pair explicitly: "Curb weight (lbs.) 3,186 (M/T) / 3,296 (DCT)" (hyundai-us-2026-elantra-n-specs). No Hyundai curb weight for the 2022 model was found, so the reference year is 2023, the earliest year with a qualifying weight at the same 276 hp rating.
